The petitioners have filed this petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1989, claiming the compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- from the respondents with regard to the death of Sagara N.H.,
in the road traffic accident that took place on 04.05.2023.
2.

The brief facts of the case of the petitioners as follows:
On 04.05.2023 at 9.35 p.m. when the deceased was travelling in the Tempo Traveller(Maxi Cab) bearing Reg. No.KA- 03-AB-4948 as passenger, near Kolinagar Bridge Outer Ring Road, Nandi Layout, Bengaluru City, at that time, the driver of the said cab drove the same in a rash and negligent manner, lost control and dashed against to the ring road center median and tree, caused the accident, due to which deceased sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the injuries.

It is further contended that, immediately after the accident, injured was shifted to Kanva Sri Sai hospital wherein he took treatment from 04.05.2023 to 13.05.2023 and inspite of better treatment, he succumbed to the injuries on 13.05.2023.

Thereafter,
the post-mortem was conducted and the dead body was handed over to the petitioners and they have performed the last rites and obsequies of the deceased by spending huge amount towards medical and funeral expenses.
3. It is further stated that the deceased was working at Kodachandri Chits and earning Rs.30,000/-
p.m. and due to his death, the petitioners are undergoing mental shock and agony and facing great financial difficulties.
The accident in question was due to the rash and negligence on the part of the driver of the offending Tempo Traveler bearing Reg. No.KA-03-AB-4948.
Hence, the 1st respondent being the owner and 2nd respondent being the insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
4. Inspite service of notice, respondent No.1 remained absent and hence he was placed exparte.
On service of summons, 2nd respondent has appeared through its learned counsel and filed objection statement.
5. The 2nd respondent in its objection statement has denied all the petition averments and contended that the petition itself is not maintainable either on facts or law.
It has denied the relationship, age, income of the deceased and the amount spent towards the medical and funeral expenses of the deceased.
It admits the issuance of policy in respect of the said offending vehicle and contended that the liability if any is subject to the terms and conditions of the policy.
Owner of the vehicle and the jurisdictional police have not complied section 134(C)and 158(6) of M.V. Act.
It has denied the alleged negligence and manner of the accident.
The compensation and interest claimed by the petitioners is excessive and exorbitant.
Hence on all these grounds, it has sought for dismissal of the petition.

6. Based on the pleadings, my predecessor in office has framed following issues:-
ISSUES Savithramma vs Nataraj.

1. Whether the petitioners prove that on 04.05.2023 at 9.35 p.m. when the deceased was travelling in the Tempo Traveller(Maxi Cab) bearing Reg. No.KA- 03-AB-4948 as passenger, near Kolinagar Bridge Outer Ring Road, Nandi Layout, Bengaluru City,
at that time, the driver of the said cab drove the same in a rash and negligent manner, lost control and dashed against to the ring road center median and tree, caused the accident, due to which deceased sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the injuries?
2. Whether the petitioners prove that they are the legal heirs of deceased Sagar N.H.?
3. Whether the petitioners are entitled for any compensation? If so, to what extent and from whom?
4. What order or Award?
7.
In order to prove the case, 1 st petitioner got examined herself as PW.1 and examined two more witnesses as PW.2 and PW.3 and got marked documents as per Ex.P1 to P28.

On the other hand,
respondents have not led their defence evidence.
8. Heard the arguments.

Issue No.1 ... In the affirmative, Issue No.2 ...
In the affirmative, Issue No.3 ...
Partly in the affirmative, Issue No.4 ...

As per final order For the following:
REASONS 10. ISSUE No.1: It is the case of the petitioners that, on 04.05.2023 at 9.35 p.m. when the deceased was travelling in the Tempo Traveller(Maxi Cab) bearing Reg. No.KA-03-AB- 4948 as passenger, near Kolinagar Bridge Outer Ring Road, Nandi Layout, Bengaluru City, at that time, the driver of the said cab drove the same in a rash and negligent manner, lost control and dashed against to the ring road center median and tree, as a result vehicle got completely collapased,
caused the accident, due to which deceased sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the injuries.
It is further contended that, immediately after the accident, injured was shifted to Kanva Sri Sai hospital and during the treatment injures was succumbed to the injuries.
It is specifically urged that, the accident occurred due the rash and negligent act of the driver of Tempo Traveler and as such the respondents are liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.

11. In order to substantiate the contentions of the petitioners, the petitioner No.2 stepped into the witness box and filed her affidavit-in-lieu of oral examination-in-chief as PW1 and got marked F.I.R,
F.I.S, spot mahazar, IMV Report, sketch, 133 notice and reply, Inquest Report, P.M. Report and charge sheet as per Ex.P1 to Ex.P10.

Also examined PW.3 Medical Record Incharge of Kanva Sri Sai hospital and he has produced the documents at Ex.P25 to 28 which are authorization letter, Police Savithramma vs Nataraj.S on 3 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/143659606/
4 intimation, MLC register extract inpatient case sheet.

sentences.text: On the other hand, respondents have not led their defence evidence.
12. This issue revolves round the sphere and ambit as to the alleged rash and negligence on the part of the driver of Tempo Traveler.
The factum of negligence has to be proved like any other fact in issue.
Before dwelling into analyzing the factum of alleged negligence, it is relevant to have the conceptual aspects pertaining to factum of negligence.
There are four basic elements that a person has to fulfill in order to do a negligent act.
These elements are as follows:
Duty: For committing a negligent act, there must be some duty on the part of the defendant.
Here it is important to understand whether the defendant has taken legal duty of care towards the plaintiff.
Breach of Duty:
After fulfilling the first criteria the plaintiff must prove that the defendant has breached the legal duty imposed on him/her.
It talks about the breach of duty on the part of the defendant which he/ she is expected to do as he/ she has some legal duty towards the plaintiff.
The action of causing something:
It means that the damage caused to the plaintiff is due to the act of the defendant.
Here the defendant may do an act which is not expected from him/her or the defendant may be negligent in not doing an act which was expected from him/ her.

Damages: At last what matters is, there must be some damage/injury that is caused to the plaintiff and this damages should be the direct consequence of the defendant's act.
Negligence means a breach of duty caused by omission to do something which has reasonable man guide by those consideration which ordinarily regulated conduct of human affairs would do which a prudent man would not do.
In common prevalence negligence connoted to the want of proper care and the rashness conveys the idea of recklessness or the doing of an act without due consideration.

13. According to the version of petitioners the accident happened when the deceased Sagara N.H.
was proceeding on the Tempo Traveler bearing Reg. No.KA-03-AB-4948 as a passenger, near Kolinagar Bridge Outer Ring Road, Nandi Layout, Bengaluru City, at that time, the driver of the said cab drove the same in a rash and negligent manner, lost control and dashed against to the ring road center median and tree, as a result vehicle got completely collapsed, caused the accident.

It is pertinent to note that, the criminal law was set in motion on the same day of accident as per Ex.P.2.
Ex.P.1 FIR has its germane in Ex.
P.2. The document which sheds light on the factum of negligence are Ex.P.3 being the Spot Mahazar and Ex.P4 Sketch prepared at the time of mahazar.

On close perusal of the Ex.P.3 and Ex.P4 it reflects that deceased was proceeding as a passenger in Tempo Traveler, the driver of said Tempo Traveler by driving it in a rash and negligent manner, lost control over the vehicle, and dashed to the centre median and tree, as a result vehicle got completely Savithramma vs Nataraj.S on 3 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/143659606/
5 collapsed and caused to accident.
The said factum is also fortified with the IMV report.
If the driver of Tempo Traveler proceeded in a normal speed, then he would certainly avoided the accident.
Added more, the contents of the IMV report itself discloses that there are no mechanical defects whatsoever in the offending vehicle.
Further more even, the chargesheet as per Ex.P10 was also filed as against the driver of the Tempo Traveler.

When such is the case having regard to Ex.P.3, 4 and IMV report coupled with Ex.P.10 charge sheet it is crystal clear that, the accident happened because of rash and negligent driving of the Tempo Traveler by its driver.

14. It is necessary to reassert that in a claim for compensation filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the claimant is expected to prove the incident on basis of principle of preponderance of probabilities and the view taken by this Court is fortified by the decision rendered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others which is reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319.

entities.text: Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Further the Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others reported in (2009) 13 SCC 530 has observed that, it is necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.

entities.text: Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others reported in (2009) 13 SCC 530
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The claimants are merely required to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied.

Further the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Krishnappa and another reported in 2001 ACJ 1105, where the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka considering the fact that the driver of the offending vehicle was not examined to prove any contributory negligence on the part of scooterist held that the accident had occurred due to rash or negligent driving by the driver of the offending vehicle.

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Krishnappa and another reported in 2001 ACJ 1105
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Even in the instant case the driver of the motorcycle is not examined to show that there was no negligence on his part and even otherwise the IO, as already observed, has clearly opined that the accident occurred only due to the fault of the driver of the motorcycle and he was charge sheeted.

15. Further though PW.1 was cross examined by respondent counsel at length, nothing has been elicited from her mouth with regard to the negligence on the part of deceased and on the other hand,
the petitioners with the help of Ex.P3, P4 coupled with Ex.P10 clearly demonstrated that there is negligence on the part of offending vehicle driver.
Viewed from any angle this court does not find any reason to distrust the version of the petitioners herein.
The discussion supra makes it is abundantly clear that, the accident occurred solely due to the rash negligent driving of the Tempo Traveller (Maxi Cab) bearing Reg. No.KA-03-AB-4948 by its driver.
As such, this Tribunal answers issue No.1 In the Affirmative.
16. Issue No.2 and 3:

While answering issue No.1, I have already observed that the death of Sagara N.H. was occurred due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of offending Tempo Traveler bearing Reg. No.KA-03-AB-4948.
Therefore, the petitioners are entitled for the compensation.
The petitioners are stated to be the mother and sister of the deceased.

6 17.

sentences.text: The petitioners
in order to prove that their relationship with the deceased Sagara N.H., examined the 1 st petitioner as PW-1.

She filed affidavit as her examination in chief and produced the copy of aadhar cards, PAN cards, driving licence marked as Ex.P11 to 17 disclosed that the 1 st petitioner is the mother and 2nd petitioner is the sister of deceased.
The respondents have not denied the say of the petitioners.
These documents demonstrates that the petitioners are the legal heirs of the deceased.
18. The petitioners have contended that the deceased was aged 23 years at the time of accident.
The petitioners have produced the notarized copy of Aadhaar card of the deceased at Ex.P11 which shows the date of birth as 01.01.2000.
The accident was occurred in the year 2023.
Hence, the age of the deceased at the time of accident was 23 years.

Further, the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case rendered in National Insurance Co., Ltd., vs. Pranay Sethi and others ((2017) 16 SCC 680) has held that, age of the deceased is basis for applying the multiplier.

entities.text: National Insurance Co., Ltd., vs. Pranay Sethi and others ((2017) 16 SCC 680)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Hence, considering the age of the deceased, the multiplier applicable to the age of 23 years is 18.
19.
The petitioners have contended that the deceased was working as employee at Kodachadri Chits and earning Rs.30,000/- per month.

On order to prove the same, petitioners have examined the HR Manager, Kodachandri Chits Pvt. Ltd., as PW.2 and he got marked salary certificates, offer letters and officer acceptance letter at Ex.P22 to 24.
The documents produced by the petitioners, as well as PW.2 depicts that deceased was permanent employee of the company and he was earning a fixed salary of Rs.19,500/- per month.
Hence, this court has taken fixed salary of Rs.19,500/- into consideration for calculation of loss of dependency.
Further the salary slip does not reflect deduction of PF/savings/IT.
As per the income tax slab for the year 2022-23, income of the deceased does not fall within the slab for deduction of income tax.

Hence, the annual income of the deceased comes to Rs.2,34,000/- p.a. (19,500x12).
20.

In view of principles laid down in the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court rendered in the case of National Insurance Co., Ltd., vs. Pranay Sethi and others ((2017) 16 SCC 680), as deceased was below the age of 40 years and was on fixed salary, an addition of 40% of the actual salary towards future prospectus is to be considered.

entities.text: National Insurance Co., Ltd., vs. Pranay Sethi and others ((2017) 16 SCC 680)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: An addition of 40% on the annual income of Rs.2,34,000/- comes to Rs.93,600/-.
In the case on hand, the deceased died leaving behind 2 dependents and he was a bachelor.

As per principle laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Sarla Varma vs. Delhi Transport Corporation (2009 ACJ 1298)., 50%(1/2) of his income is required to be deducted towards his personal expenses which comes to Rs.1,63,800/- per annum (Rs.3,27,600 - Rs.1,63,800/-)
21.

entities.text: Sarla Varma vs. Delhi Transport Corporation (2009 ACJ 1298)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The income of the deceased is taken as Rs.1,63,800/- p.a. and the multiplier '18' is applied, then the loss of dependency comes to Rs.29,48,400/- (Rs.1,63,800 X 18).
Considering the above facts, this Tribunal deems it just and reasonable to grant for compensation of Rs.29,48,400/- under the head of Loss of dependency.

7 22.
In this case, petitioner No.1 and 2 are mother and unmarried sister of the deceased.

As per the decision reported in (2018) 12 SCC 130 between Magma General Insurance Company Limited V/s Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram and others, the petitioners are entitled for filial consortium, as the filial consortium is the right of the parents and family members to compensation in the case of an accidental death of a child.

entities.text: Magma General Insurance Company Limited V/s Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: An accident leading to the death of a child causes great shock and agony to the parents and family of the deceased.
The greatest agony for a parent is to lose of their child during their lifetime.
Children are valued for their love, affection, companionship and their oral in the family unit.
Therefore, petitioner No.1 and 2 are entitled for Rs.44,000/- each under the head of Filial consortium.

23. Further, as law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex court in National Insurance company Vs Pranay Sethi and others, the compensation towards loss to the estate, funeral expenses and consortium to be awarded.

entities.text: National Insurance company Vs Pranay Sethi and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence this Tribunal award Rs.18,150/- towards loss to estate and Rs.18,150/- towards funeral expenses as enhanced at the rate of 10% on every 3 years.
24. Medical expenses:
Petitioners have produced medical bills to the tune of Rs.5,44,713/- at Ex.P19.

On perusal of said bills it reflects that deceased was admitted at Kanva Sri Sai hospital immediately after the accident on 04.05.2023 and on 13.05.2023 he expired in the hospital during the period of treatment.

Hence, there is no reason to disbelieve the said medical bills, hence petitioners are entitled for Rs.5,44,713/-
under the above head.

25. The calculation table stands as follows :
 Compensation heads Compensation  amount (Rs.)
 1. Towards loss of dependency 29,48,400/-
 2. Towards loss of Filial 88,000/-
 Consortium to the petitioner No.1  and 2 (44,000x2)

3 . Towards loss to Estate 18,150/-
4. Towards transportation of dead 18,150/-
 body funeral and obsequies  ceremony expenses  5.

Medical Expenses 5,44,713/-
 Total 36,17,413/-
In all the petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs.36,17,413/-.

8 26.
As regard the apportionment of the compensation, petitioners No.1 is mother and petitioner No.2 is sister of the deceased.

Therefore out of the total compensation, the petitioners No. 1 and 2 are entitled for compensation at the ratio of 75:25.
27.
The petitioners are claiming interest on the compensation amount.
The respondents have denied the same.

Our Hon'ble High Court in the case rendered in Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others Vs Ulrich Belchior Fernandes and another (MFA.No.100090/2014 C/W MFA.No.25107/2013 dated 07.03.2018), has held that in the absence of any other law relating to interest on judgments, the MACT has to follow the provisions of Sec.34 of C.P.C and awarded interest @ 6% per annum.

entities.text: Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others Vs Ulrich Belchior Fernandes and another (MFA.No.100090/2014 C/W MFA.No.25107/2013 dated
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Considering the aforesaid decision, I deem it proper to award interest at 6% per annum on the above compensation amount.
28. Liability:

Regarding fixation of liability is concerned, I have already observed that the accident was taken place due to the negligence on the part of the driver of offending Tempo Traveler bearing Reg. No.KA-03-AB-4948.
It is not in dispute that 1st respondent is the owner of the offending vehicle.
The respondents have not proved the breach of any of the policy conditions.
Hence, 1 st respondent being the owner and 2nd respondent being the insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
The 2nd respondent shall indemnify the 1st respondent in payment of compensation amount.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 in the Affirmative and Issue No.3 Partly in the Affirmative.
29. Issue No.4:

In view of my findings on issues No.1 to 3, I pass the following:
ORDER
The petition is allowed in part with cost.

The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs. 36,17,413/- (Rupees Thirty six lakhs seventeen thousand four hundred and thirteen only) with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent No.2 is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of one month from the date of award.

On deposit of the award amount together with interest, the claimants are entitled for the compensation amount by way of apportionment as follows :
Petitioner No.1 - 75% Petitioner No.2 - 25% Out of the share amount of Petitioner No.1 and 2 a sum equal to 25% shall be deposited in their respective names in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank of their choice for a period of 3 years and the remaining 75% shall be released to them through E-payment on proper identification and verification.
However the said petitioners are at liberty to withdraw the periodical interest accrued on the deposit amount from time to time.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.

1. Whether the petitioners prove that on 04.05.2023 at 9.35 p.m. when the deceased was travelling in the Tempo Traveller(Maxi Cab) bearing Reg. No.KA- 03-AB-4948 as passenger, near Kolinagar Bridge Outer Ring Road, Nandi Layout, Bengaluru City,
at that time, the driver of the said cab drove the same in a rash and negligent manner, lost control and dashed against to the ring road center median and tree, caused the accident, due to which deceased sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the injuries?
2. Whether the petitioners prove that they are the legal heirs of deceased Sagar N.H.?
3. Whether the petitioners are entitled for any compensation? If so, to what extent and from whom?
4. What order or Award?
7.
As per final order For the following:
REASONS 10. ISSUE No.1: It is the case of the petitioners that, on 04.05.2023 at 9.35 p.m. when the deceased was travelling in the Tempo Traveller(Maxi Cab) bearing Reg. No.KA-03-AB- 4948 as passenger, near Kolinagar Bridge Outer Ring Road, Nandi Layout, Bengaluru City, at that time, the driver of the said cab drove the same in a rash and negligent manner, lost control and dashed against to the ring road center median and tree, as a result vehicle got completely collapased,
caused the accident, due to which deceased sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the injuries.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
In common prevalence negligence connoted to the want of proper care and the rashness conveys the idea of recklessness or the doing of an act without due consideration.
When such is the case having regard to Ex.P.3, 4 and IMV report coupled with Ex.P.10 charge sheet it is crystal clear that, the accident happened because of rash and negligent driving of the Tempo Traveler by its driver.
The claimants are merely required to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied.
Further the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Krishnappa and another reported in 2001 ACJ 1105, where the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka considering the fact that the driver of the offending vehicle was not examined to prove any contributory negligence on the part of scooterist held that the accident had occurred due to rash or negligent driving by the driver of the offending vehicle.
Even in the instant case the driver of the motorcycle is not examined to show that there was no negligence on his part and even otherwise the IO, as already observed, has clearly opined that the accident occurred only due to the fault of the driver of the motorcycle and he was charge sheeted.
15. Further though PW.1 was cross examined by respondent counsel at length, nothing has been elicited from her mouth with regard to the negligence on the part of deceased and on the other hand,
the petitioners with the help of Ex.P3, P4 coupled with Ex.P10 clearly demonstrated that there is negligence on the part of offending vehicle driver.
Further, the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case rendered in National Insurance Co., Ltd., vs. Pranay Sethi and others ((2017) 16 SCC 680) has held that, age of the deceased is basis for applying the multiplier.
Hence, this court has taken fixed salary of Rs.19,500/- into consideration for calculation of loss of dependency.
Further the salary slip does not reflect deduction of PF/savings/IT.
As per the income tax slab for the year 2022-23, income of the deceased does not fall within the slab for deduction of income tax.
Hence, the annual income of the deceased comes to Rs.2,34,000/- p.a. (19,500x12).
20.
In the case on hand, the deceased died leaving behind 2 dependents and he was a bachelor.
Considering the above facts, this Tribunal deems it just and reasonable to grant for compensation of Rs.29,48,400/- under the head of Loss of dependency.
Savithramma vs Nataraj.S on 3 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/143659606/
7 22.
In this case, petitioner No.1 and 2 are mother and unmarried sister of the deceased.
As per the decision reported in (2018) 12 SCC 130 between Magma General Insurance Company Limited V/s Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram and others, the petitioners are entitled for filial consortium, as the filial consortium is the right of the parents and family members to compensation in the case of an accidental death of a child.
An accident leading to the death of a child causes great shock and agony to the parents and family of the deceased.
The greatest agony for a parent is to lose of their child during their lifetime.
opennyai_summary.arguments: 14. It is necessary to reassert that in a claim for compensation filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the claimant is expected to prove the incident on basis of principle of preponderance of probabilities and the view taken by this Court is fortified by the decision rendered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others which is reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319.
opennyai_summary.decision:
Hence this Tribunal award Rs.18,150/- towards loss to estate and Rs.18,150/- towards funeral expenses as enhanced at the rate of 10% on every 3 years.
25. The calculation table stands as follows :
 Compensation heads Compensation  amount (Rs.)
 1. Towards loss of dependency 29,48,400/-
 2. Towards loss of Filial 88,000/-
 Consortium to the petitioner No.1  and 2 (44,000x2)
Medical Expenses 5,44,713/-
 Total 36,17,413/-
In all the petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs.36,17,413/-.
Considering the aforesaid decision, I deem it proper to award interest at 6% per annum on the above compensation amount.
The respondents have not proved the breach of any of the policy conditions.
Hence, 1 st respondent being the owner and 2nd respondent being the insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
The 2nd respondent shall indemnify the 1st respondent in payment of compensation amount.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 in the Affirmative and Issue No.3 Partly in the Affirmative.
29. Issue No.4:
In view of my findings on issues No.1 to 3, I pass the following:
ORDER
The petition is allowed in part with cost.
The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs. 36,17,413/- (Rupees Thirty six lakhs seventeen thousand four hundred and thirteen only) with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent No.2 is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of one month from the date of award.
On deposit of the award amount together with interest, the claimants are entitled for the compensation amount by way of apportionment as follows :
Petitioner No.1 - 75% Petitioner No.2 - 25% Out of the share amount of Petitioner No.1 and 2 a sum equal to 25% shall be deposited in their respective names in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank of their choice for a period of 3 years and the remaining 75% shall be released to them through E-payment on proper identification and verification.
However the said petitioners are at liberty to withdraw the periodical interest accrued on the deposit amount from time to time.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
